entries.text: All that we are is the result of what we have thought. The mind is everything. What we think we become.
He is able who thinks he is able.
Better than a thousand hollow words is one word that brings peace.
You yourself, as much as anybody in the entire universe, deserve your love and affection.
Hatred does not cease by hatred, but only by love; this is the eternal rule.
There is no fire like passion, no shark like hatred, no snare like folly, no torrent like greed.
Those who are free of resentful thoughts surely find peace.
Do not dwell in the past, do not dream of the future, concentrate the mind on the present moment.
Better it is to live one day seeing the rise and fall of things than to live a hundred years without ever seeing it.
The mind is restless and difficult to restrain, but it is subdued by meditation.
Let us live happily, free from hatred in the midst of those who hate.
An insincere and evil friend is more to be feared than a wild beast; a wild beast may wound your body, but an evil friend will wound your mind.
Drop by drop is the water pot filled. Likewise, the wise man, gathering it little by little, fills himself with good.
The fool who knows he is a fool is that much wiser. A fool who thinks he is wise is a fool indeed.
The one who has conquered himself is a far greater hero than he who has defeated a thousand times a thousand men.
Just as a solid rock is not shaken by the storm, even so the wise are not affected by praise or blame.
Health is the greatest gift, contentment the greatest wealth, faithfulness the best relationship.
Even as the fletcher whittles and makes straight his arrows, so does the discerning man straighten his trembling and unsteady thoughts.
Though one may conquer a thousand times a thousand men in battle, yet he indeed is the noblest victor who conquers himself.
Let go of anger. Let go of pride. When you are bound by nothing you go beyond sorrow.
From craving arises sorrow; from craving arises fear. For those who are wholly free from craving, there is no sorrow; whence, then, fear?
Do not look at what others do or fail to do. Look only at what you yourself do and fail to do.
We are what we think. All that we are arises with our thoughts. With our thoughts we make the world.
A disciplined mind brings happiness.
Quieten your mind. Empty your mind. Be still. Let the war of thoughts subside.
As rain does not break through a well-thatched roof, passion will not break through a well-reflecting mind.
Do not what is evil. Do what is good. Keep your mind pure. This is the teaching of Buddha.
Whatever a mother, father or any other kinsman may do for us, a well-directed mind does us greater service.
The one who has tamed the mind, which is difficult to tame, fickle and wanders at will, is truly blessed.
By oneself is evil done; by oneself one suffers. By oneself evil is left undone; by oneself is one purified.
If anything is worth doing, do it with all your heart.
Peace comes from within. Do not seek it without.
It is better to travel well than to arrive.
Thousands of candles can be lit from a single candle, and the life of the candle will not be shortened. Happiness never decreases by being shared.
Speak only endearing speech, speech that is welcomed. Speech which brings no evil to others is a pleasant thing.
Just as a mother would protect her only child with her life, even so let one cultivate a boundless love towards all beings.
There is no path to happiness. Happiness is the path.
All wrong-doing arises because of mind. If mind is transformed, can wrong-doing remain?
In the end only three things matter: how much you loved, how gently you lived, and how gracefully you let go of things not meant for you.
Irrigators channel waters; fletchers straighten arrows; carpenters bend wood; the wise master themselves.
